research.question: Do explicit boundaries preserve correct behavior under an unavailable dependency?

briefs.what: Resilience uses bounded retry, timeout, breaker state and explicitly permitted read fallback.
briefs.when: Use the router for eligible reads when cloud context may be slow or unavailable.
briefs.when_not: Do not retry invalid input or redirect an approved live mutation.
briefs.why: A workshop can remain usable during outages without misrepresenting local results as live.

briefs.expected_result: The handoff names verified properties, missing evidence and accountable owners.
briefs.failure_and_recovery: An unmet gate remains a blocker or explicit scope exclusion, not a success-shaped fallback.
how: Review the threat model and owners.
Verify identity and permission-negative cases.
Define rollout and rollback evidence.
Track incomplete tenant and CI checks explicitly.

research.baseline: Reviewed access decisions and global authority invariants.
evolution: Single dependencies expose callers directly to failures.
Routing introduces bounded retries and failure state.
Explicit fallback preserves a permitted read experience.
Governed writes bind approval to the exact destination and never redirect.
research.experiment: Define a synthetic access matrix before testing. Compare allowed and denied requests, gateway acceptance with backend refusal, and narrowing with attempted-widening overlays. Record local contract results separately from any approved tenant validation.

foundations.application: Use timeouts, bounded retries, circuit breakers and explicit unavailable or permitted fallback results.
foundations.explanation: A dependency failure should have a bounded blast radius and a defined caller-visible outcome.

foundations.application: An available local answer cannot certify live execution; a successful write cannot establish that it was authorized.
foundations.explanation: Availability, correctness and authorization are separate properties and cannot substitute for each other.

research.hypothesis: Independent negative-access, gateway-policy and overlay-restriction tests expose authority gaps that a successful demo request cannot detect.
limitations: Fault injection is not a real tenant outage or recovery drill.
Successful offline tests do not establish production network or identity configuration.
research.question: Which prototype observations fail to establish production safety or reliability?

briefs.what: Production readiness combines identity, networking, data ownership, evaluation, cost and operational recovery.
briefs.when: Use the checklist when moving a bounded prototype toward an operated service.
briefs.when_not: Do not mark documented components or deferred GitHub checks as live-verified.
briefs.why: A passing local demo and an active capacity do not certify a secure reliable deployment.

briefs.expected_result: The chosen boundary has a reason, an independent routing baseline and explicit per-domain authorization.
briefs.failure_and_recovery: Ambiguity requires clarification; denied access must not retry through an administrator or unrestricted domain.
how: Define domain vocabulary and permitted facts.
Create expected route and denial cases.
Compare deterministic routing with one bounded agent.
Add agents only for demonstrated lifecycle or policy differences.

research.baseline: Independently authored expected route and access decisions.
evolution: Sequence models generate from learned patterns and context.
Retrieval augments model parameters with selected external information.
Tool loops incorporate observations from an environment.
Product harnesses add identity
policies and evaluation around the loop.
research.experiment: Compare deterministic routing, one bounded agent and a reviewed multi-agent candidate on the same held-out synthetic requests, identities and tools. Stratify ambiguous and denied cases; record failures and overhead.

foundations.application: Do not infer numeric correctness, tool execution or permission from the fluency of an assistant response.
foundations.explanation: Attention-based sequence modeling supports generation, but does not itself verify external facts or execute operations.

foundations.application: Select relevant context, record actual tool results and score the final answer independently of the model.
foundations.explanation: RAG studies external retrieved information; ReAct studies interleaving processing with actions and observations.

research.hypothesis: For distinct tool and ownership boundaries, a bounded domain arrangement improves route accuracy compared with one unconstrained agent; for simple vocabulary routing it may only add overhead.
limitations: A local router cannot establish language-model routing performance.
Synthetic tests do not certify preview Fabric IQ identity propagation.
research.question: Does agent decomposition improve domain routing without increasing unauthorized disclosure?

briefs.what: Domain ownership, bounded tools and independently managed agents are different architectural boundaries.
briefs.when: Use this comparison when one workflow needs context from several governed business domains.
briefs.when_not: Do not add a coordinator when a deterministic router or one bounded agent meets the contract.
briefs.why: Splitting by department alone adds coordination and access risks without proving a benefit.

briefs.expected_result: Quality, context age and repeated effects are measured independently; actions remain reviewed proposals.
briefs.failure_and_recovery: Reject malformed or stale context explicitly and apply bounded retries without duplicate authoritative effects.
how: Define the enrichment schema and independent labels.
Define event keys and freshness policy.
Compare candidate output with fixed references.
Test duplicates and out-of-order replay before considering live execution.

research.baseline: Reviewed synthetic class labels and predefined event-state transitions.
evolution: Batch transformations create reusable derived facts.
Model enrichment introduces quality and version uncertainty.
Streams introduce late and duplicate events.
Agent triage adds proposals without transferring write authority.
research.experiment: Use fixed synthetic labels and events. Compare candidate enrichment with reviewed labels, then compare ordered, delayed and duplicate replay with independently expected states and proposals. Keep inputs and rules fixed.

foundations.application: Persist lineage and evaluate labels independently of the candidate.
foundations.explanation: An interpreted field depends on its source and transformation version, not merely its output type.

foundations.application: Define freshness, late-event rules and stable event keys before triage.
foundations.explanation: Occurrence order can differ from arrival order, and repeated delivery must not repeat an authoritative effect.

research.hypothesis: Independent labels and duplicate/late-event tests detect incorrect interpretation or repeated effects even when every processing call reports success.
limitations: Deterministic enrichment cannot establish model classification performance.
Small replay sequences do not establish production throughput or delivery guarantees.
research.question: Do explicit quality and event-time contracts expose errors hidden by successful pipeline completion?

briefs.what: Batch enrichment stores versioned derived data; event triage uses timely context to propose a response.
briefs.when: Use enrichment for reusable interpretation and event context when timeliness changes the decision.
briefs.when_not: Keep deterministic thresholds and calculations outside a model when they already solve the task.
briefs.why: Model quality and temporal correctness need separate contracts, references and recovery rules.

briefs.expected_result: Every promised outcome maps to an observable test, and remaining gaps are recorded.
briefs.failure_and_recovery: A contradictory specification needs clarification; generated instructions must not overwrite repository authority.
how: Use the repository spec-driven-delivery Skill.
Specify outcomes and exclusions.
Review requirement quality and task dependencies.
Implement reviewed local work and verify convergence.
Treat any cloud mutation as a separately approved change.

research.baseline: The reviewed specification and independent acceptance tests.
evolution: Completions assist local edits.
Repository instructions constrain conventions and contracts.
Skills provide repeatable domain procedures.
MCP supplies bounded observed context.
Governed review ties changes to approvals and verification.
research.experiment: Compare a bounded synthetic feature checklist with requirement-to-test traceability on the same candidate implementation. Review omitted adverse cases without changing the acceptance criteria after seeing the result.

foundations.application: Reconcile candidate Silver transformations and DAX with the same committed synthetic baseline.
foundations.explanation: A generated artifact must be judged against an independent behavioral contract, not its author's confidence.

foundations.application: Compare instructions, Skills and read-only MCP context separately instead of changing all of them and the model at once.
foundations.explanation: Removing one component while holding other conditions fixed helps isolate its contribution under the tested conditions.

research.hypothesis: Requirements linked to independent tests expose implementation gaps that a task-completion checklist misses.
limitations: Observed timing is task-specific rather than a product benchmark.
Claude Code remains documented-only unless an actual comparable run is recorded.
research.question: Does explicit acceptance traceability reduce missing behavior in a cross-layer prototype?

briefs.what: Spec-driven delivery links a user outcome to reviewed requirements, a design, tasks and independent convergence.
briefs.when: Use the full workflow for a new use case, ambiguous requirements or changes across data, API, UI and governance.
briefs.when_not: Do not require Spec Kit for a typo, narrow repair or normal execution of an existing demo.
briefs.why: Cross-layer PoCs fail when a convincing implementation replaces the original acceptance criteria.

evidence.label: LIVE
limitations: Recorded state is not current capacity health.
Resource existence does not prove notebook execution or Power BI publication.
No resource was created by this verification.

evidence.label: LIVE
limitations: Readiness GETs are not model inference evidence.
This does not certify production identity or current service availability.
No new deployment was performed by these checks.
evidence.scope: Read-only checks passed for the existing resource, project, model deployment, data plane, agent and Fabric connection. Foundry supplies reasoning and orchestration over governed context.
evidence.title: Foundry project, model deployment and existing agent

evidence.label: LIVE
limitations: The resources already existed; this session did not deploy replacements.
Configuration alone does not prove telemetry ingestion.
An ingestion cap is not a guaranteed total spending limit.
evidence.provider: Azure Resource Manager and Azure Monitor
evidence.scope: Existing workspace-based monitoring resources were observed with Succeeded provisioning, 30-day retention and a one GB/day ingestion cap. Foundry monitoring connections and allLogs/AllMetrics diagnostics were present.
evidence.title: Application Insights and Log Analytics

evidence.label: LIVE
limitations: The span payload is synthetic; cloud ingestion was LIVE.
This is client telemetry, not a newly verified Foundry agent trace.
An initial exporter warning was corrected before ingestion verification.

evidence.scope: An aggregate query observed two matching synthetic span records after ingestion delay. This demonstrates actual cloud ingestion, not merely configured monitoring.

evidence.label: LIVE
limitations: Historical observation rather than a current health check.
Not Fabric MCP invocation or Guide 1 write evidence.

limitations: The Fabric tool is PREVIEW.
Not fresh five-case certification or delivery evidence.
Server-side agent trace ingestion remains unverified.

limitations: A configured provider is not a verified connection.
Checkpoint notes are not automatic proof of tool execution.

evidence.label: LOCAL
limitations: Not evidence of cloud scheduling or delivery.
The screenshot predates the workshop redesign.
evidence.scope: Synthetic interface showing the second use case and shared runtime configuration.
evidence.title: Grounded-agent use-case UI

execution_paths.description: Build and learn with synthetic data and deterministic providers without Azure access.
execution_paths.fallback: No live call is attempted, so there is no cloud fallback.
prerequisites: The repository's locked local dependencies and synthetic data.
execution_paths.results: Reads are LOCAL; governed write rehearsals are SIMULATED. Offline does not mean an actual Fabric workspace was changed.
execution_paths.safety: No Azure credentials or active Fabric capacity are required. The offline demo must report zero cloud operations.
execution_paths.title: Local / offline

execution_paths.description: The default application tries eligible live reads first and keeps learning usable through explicitly permitted local read fallback.
execution_paths.fallback: Only eligible reads may fall back to LOCAL, with a disclosed reason. An approved LIVE write never redirects.
prerequisites: Private Azure/Fabric/Foundry bindings in ignored .env configuration.
Available capacity and services for the connected path.
execution_paths.results: Each operation reports LIVE, PREVIEW or LOCAL according to what actually ran, with provider and fallback evidence.
execution_paths.safety: The connected demo can consume model usage; active Fabric capacity incurs billing. Live mutations remain disabled by default and need separate approval.
execution_paths.title: Azure / Fabric live-first

execution_paths.description: Require the connected providers to perform the bounded verification instead of accepting a local answer.
execution_paths.fallback: LOCAL fallback cannot satisfy the strict live gate. Unavailable or incorrect connected results fail verification.
prerequisites: The same private bindings and Entra permissions as the live-first path.
Available Fabric capacity and the configured existing Foundry agent.
execution_paths.results: The demo checks an actual Fabric read and a baseline-reconciled synthetic Foundry answer; the Fabric agent tool is labeled PREVIEW.
execution_paths.safety: This performs a bounded cloud read and model question, not deployment or publication. Model usage and capacity can cost money; consequential writes need a separate approved plan.
execution_paths.title: Strict Azure / Fabric live verification

content.execution_summary: You can learn entirely offline, use the live-first application with disclosed read fallback, or require strict connected verification. Running the UI or a server on your computer does not mean its data operations are offline. The application uses Fabric REST and Foundry SDK; coding clients use the separately configured real Fabric MCP server.

Claude Code is DOCUMENTED ONLY in the bake-off.
Production identity and deployment gates are not certified by this prototype.

Reconcile the answer against an independent baseline.
Produce a reviewed synthetic brief and explain the limits of web context and proposed corrections.

Web grounding needs licensing and boundary review; never send confidential figures in queries.
Fresh server-side trace verification remains open.
